draft.title: The cross-cultural component
card: The PIP must include a cross-cultural component. This means the student compares the topic across more than one culture, group or time.
The comparison can be between countries, between groups within one society, or between the past and the present.
The aim is to show how experiences of the topic differ, and to explain why. Describing each culture on its own is not enough.
For example, a student studying teenage part-time work might compare how teenagers in Australia and in Japan experience it, and then explain what causes the differences.
draft.remember: Compare the topic across cultures, groups or times, and show how and why experiences differ.

a.q: What must the cross-cultural component of the PIP do?
opts: Compare the topic across cultures, groups or times
Describe one culture in as much detail as possible
Survey people from one group about their opinions
List facts about the topic in several countries
a.why: The component is about comparing, so the student must set the topic side by side across cultures, groups or times and show how experiences differ. Describing one culture, or listing facts, does not compare anything.
a.clue: Think about what you do with two cases, not just how many you cover.

b.q: Priya studies how young people use social media. She writes a detailed section on teenagers in Sydney, then a separate section on teenagers in Seoul, but never links them. What is missing?
opts: A comparison showing how and why experiences differ
A larger sample of teenagers from Sydney
A second topic that is easier to compare
A section on how she feels about social media
b.why: Priya covers two cultures, but she only describes each one. The component needs her to compare them, showing how experiences differ and explaining why. More Sydney data would not fix this, because the gap is the missing comparison.
b.clue: Covering two places is not the same as comparing them.

a.best: Compare the topic across cultures, groups or times

b.best: A comparison showing how and why experiences differ

check.summary: No problems found. The card's inclusion of past versus present as a cross-cultural comparison matches the chapter outline, but it may be worth checking against current NESA PIP guidance, which treats continuity and change as a separate requirement.
